requirement: In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline or fenced, MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. A fenced reference MUST render its badge followed by its body as Markdown. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. Badges MAY be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a fenced reference's badge and body MAY be visually set apart from the surrounding text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge MAY show a help cursor to signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.
rationale: **Judgment:** `requirements.references.book_badges` is met. The implementation is marked completely and exactly. The tests cover the main points of the design space. **Implementation** - **Reference badges.** - `reference_badge` in `src/lib.rs` builds the badge for each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference. - It calls `shield_badge`, which produces a Shields.io static badge `` with alt text "` `". - `ReferenceKind::label` and `ReferenceKind::color` supply the role text and colour. - A project definition gets an `` linking to the definition's anchor, `habeas-req-…` or `habeas-example-…`. - A built-in gets an unlinked `` whose title is its full text. - Terms and unknown names return `None`, so they stay literal. - **Cross-chapter and nested links.** `chapter_href` computes relative paths, including `../` from nested chapters. `DefinitionKind::anchor` produces the target id, which `replace_definitions` emits on the definition's badge. - **Fenced references.** - `fenced::markdown_fences` (with `MarkdownFence`) finds the fences. Fences in code or raw HTML stay literal. - `replace_references` emits the badge, then the body. It recurses on the body, so the body is rendered as Markdown with nested references handled. - Unclosed or invalid fences are skipped and stay literal. - `replace_inline_references` handles the inline form. - **Definition badges.** `replace_definitions` renders each valid fenced `{req}` or `{example}` as a Shields.io badge whose label is the kind (`DefinitionKind::badge`). Invalid names, unclosed blocks and code examples stay literal, so text outside directives is untouched. - **CSS.** `md/habeas.css` is anchored with `:impl:`. - Visited links share the unvisited rule (`color: inherit`). - `:focus-visible` shows an outline. - Hover only applies `filter: brightness(1.08)`, which the requirement allows. - The inline layout, the fenced-reference block styling and the `cursor: help` on built-ins are all permitted by the requirement's MAY clauses. - **No unspecified behaviour.** The extra behaviour in the marked code is covered by other requirements that are also marked: "See evidence" links by `index.navigation`, escaping by `safe_badges`, and built-in rendering by `builtin_definitions`. `preprocess_book` only orchestrates these functions, so under the `targets` rule it needs no `{impl}` mark. **Tests** - `fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked` checks: - the badge comes before the body; - the fence line is consumed; - an unlinked built-in span with its full-text title; - an inline built-in citation, an unknown name and a code example all stay literal; - a fenced reference nested in a requirement renders correctly. - `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` checks `impl`, `cite` and `test` links from `guides/deep.md` to `../requirements.html#habeas-req-…`. It also checks the badge URLs and the colour for each role. - `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` covers the definition badge for an example and cross-chapter links to example anchors. Invalid example names and code examples stay literal. - `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` and `chapter_path_prefixes_the_requirement_name` cover the `{req}` badge alt text and literal text outside directives. - `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` covers alt text and URL escaping. - `badge_stylesheet_keeps_visited_links_legible_and_shows_focus` (with `stylesheet_rules`) checks that: - visited and unvisited rules are identical; - a non-zero, non-`none` focus outline exists; - hover only brightens; - the stylesheet styles only the permitted Habeas classes. I found no acknowledged FIXMEs and no unmarked gaps.

text: In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline or fenced, MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. A fenced reference MUST render its badge followed by its body as Markdown. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. Badges MAY be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a fenced reference's badge and body MAY be visually set apart from the surrounding text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge MAY show a help cursor to signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under {cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git` and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
